QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_40

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust ran a women-SHG program with investment of INR 25 lakh. Gross monetised outcomes: INR 90 lakh. Assumptions: deadweight 20%, attribution 25%, drop-off 10%, displacement nil. Compute the SROI ratio.

explanation.text: The Logic: Standard SROI methodology applies a multiplicative cascade of adjustments to the gross monetised outcome before dividing by the investment: gross outcome is first reduced for deadweight (what would have happened anyway), then for attribution (credit to other actors), then for drop-off (fade over time), and then for displacement. Starting from INR 90 lakh gross: after deadweight 20% -> 90 x (1 - 0.20) = 72 lakh; after attribution 25% -> 72 x (1 - 0.25) = 54 lakh; after drop-off 10% -> 54 x (1 - 0.10) = 48.6 lakh; displacement is nil, so Net Impact Value = INR 48.6 lakh. SROI = 48.6 / 25 = 1.944, i.e. approximately 1.94:1 - positive but modest. The Trap: 3.60:1 is simply gross outcome / investment (90 / 25) with no adjustments. 2.88:1 applies only the deadweight deduction. 1.45:1 over-deducts (e.g., adds the percentages additively instead of multiplicatively, or double-counts a step). The correct method is the multiplicative cascade in the order deadweight -> attribution -> drop-off -> displacement. Note: The cited workbook pages (134, 135, 151, 158 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) cover SROI, baseline / counterfactual, monetisation, and disclosure requirements, but they do not, in the pages checked, explicitly write out the SROI ratio formula or the multiplicative deadweight -> attribution -> drop-off -> displacement adjustment sequence. The framing above reflects general SROI methodology as practised in social-impact evaluation; the arithmetic is internally consistent with that methodology.
